scope: Read-only launcher, existing log, ELF and filesystem metadata audit; this audit executed no QEMU, target, SDK, account or purchase operation

launcher.guest_ld_library_path: selected SYSROOT/lib followed by official RUNTIME/libs

elf.official_loader: ELF32 ARM EABI5 hard-float, ARMv7/VFPv3, SONAME ld-linux-armhf.so.3, DT_VERSYM present
elf.debian_loader: ELF32 ARM EABI5 hard-float, ARMv7/VFPv3-D16, SONAME ld-linux-armhf.so.3, DT_VERSYM present
elf.luajit: ELF32 ARM EABI5 hard-float, ARMv7/VFPv3, DT_RPATH=$ORIGIN:$ORIGIN/libs
elf.qemu_host: ELF64 x86-64 static PIE; no PT_INTERP or DT_NEEDED in the inspected file

conclusions: The recorded official-loader failure happens during loader bootstrap before downstream library search; there is no observed core-library mixture explaining this assertion.
The successful Debian probe intentionally uses Debian core runtime libraries with KOReader's RPATH-selected C++ library. It is not an all-Debian or a Kindle-glibc result.
The clean explicit process environment prevents inherited host LD_LIBRARY_PATH, LD_PRELOAD and QEMU_LD_PREFIX from explaining this launch.
QEMU -L is an interpreter/sysroot lookup prefix, not a chroot. Absolute source/runtime paths remain host-visible; no corresponding prefixed duplicate was present in the inspected directories.
The precise bootstrap assertion cause remains unresolved by this path audit. Root's existing minimal reproduction is sufficient; repeating SDK or crypto probes would not improve this boundary.
reproducibility_limits: The run script depends on externally staged ROOT/probe.lua and does not record that file's hash.
The original official execution JSON predates the current expected_glibc argument. Its command is not an exact replay recipe for the current probe, although its failure preceded Lua execution.
Debian extraction reuses its destination and does not remove extra files from a previous extraction; no conflicting core library was observed in this audit.
